sections.kicker: Prepared for Superbloom Labs by Atla · November 2026
sections.lead: We looked at your site the way a new customer would. Here is what stood out, in order of weight.
sections.thesis: Superbloom has a poetic name. The site sounds like every hangover supplement.
sections.keep: Your name. Superbloom suggests recovery as something beautiful, which no rival in the aisle does.

sections.label: Front door
title: Three things people
meet first.
Three things

pins.quote: Your 100% natural herbal solution for hangover recovery & liver support
pins.what: The headline is a category description.
pins.why: Natural, herbal and liver support is what every hangover brand says.
pins.how: Say what only Superbloom believes about the morning after.
pins.label: Your headline
pins.cost: Shoppers compare you on price per sachet.

pins.what: The scrolling line repeats a list of free from claims.
pins.why: These are table stakes, and repeating them six times makes them the brand.
pins.how: Use this strip for your voice, not for compliance.
pins.label: Your ticker
pins.cost: The page sounds like a label, not a brand.

pins.what: The name promises bloom; the site never uses it.
pins.why: A brand name that sets a mood is a rare asset in a functional aisle.
pins.how: Build the words and imagery around the bloom idea.
pins.label: Your name
pins.cost: You pay for a name and get none of its value.

sections.intro: You asked for a look at Superbloom Labs, and you said something is off even after a new website. I spent time on the site. Three things stood out.

sections.body: It is 20 minutes with me. We go through this page together, on Superbloom Labs's own screens, and you leave knowing what to change first.
sections.note: A few short questions first, then you pick a time. You can also just reply to the email.

reference: Aesop, from skincare. Its botanicals are told with a voice, so the product never reads as a commodity.
